# t13.1 — Architecture Enforcement Gap Closed + Correlation Logging Restored

**Role:** backend · **Classification:** brownfield-rewrite · **Phase:** Implementation
**Status:** ✅ complete — all three gaps closed, full build green, negative control captured.

## Summary

t13 delivered the layered rewrite but left three defects that would have let the layering
silently rot. All three are now closed:

|---|---|---|---|
| **G1** — `presentation ⊥ infrastructure` rule never existed | HIGH | Added **Rule 5b** to `LayerDependencyRulesTest` | Negative control: rule fails and names the offender (§ Negative Control) |
| **G2** — MDC correlation logging *deleted*, not migrated | HIGH | New `PropagateCorrelationPort` + `MdcCorrelationAdapter`; 2 propagation tests restored + 11 new | 892 tests green; DI wiring test proves the bean resolves |
| **G3** — duplicate `ConfigDefaults` / `RetryPolicyUtils` | MEDIUM | Consolidated into `shared`, infrastructure copies deleted, 12 call sites repointed | `grep 'class ConfigDefaults\|class RetryPolicyUtils'` → 2 files, both in `shared` |

## G1 — Architecture rule restored

**Rule 5b** was added immediately after Rule 5 so the dependency-direction rules stay contiguous
(3, 4, 5, 5b) and Rule 6a/6b keep their numbers — the `sibling-package-cycle-granularity`
learning references those by number.

```
assertNoViolations("Rule 5b (presentation ⊥ infrastructure)",
                   classesIn(PRESENTATION),
                   dep -> dep.startsWith(INFRASTRUCTURE),
                   Set.of());
```

It ships with **`Set.of()`** — zero exemptions. `assertNoViolations` asserts the violator set
*exactly equals* the exemption set, so an empty exemption set means the rule is strictly enforced.

### Negative Control

The whole point of G1 is that a rule which cannot fail is worthless. Proof it fails:

**Mutation** — added a real bytecode reference (not just an import) from `presentation.CliOutput`:

```java
static final Class<?> ARCH_PROBE = MdcCorrelationAdapter.class;
```

**Result:**

```
[arch] Rule 5b (presentation ⊥ infrastructure)            69 classes inspected, 1 violator(s), 0 exempt
[ERROR] LayerDependencyRulesTest.presentationDependsOnNoInfrastructure:240->assertNoViolations:382
Rule 5b (presentation ⊥ infrastructure)
  dev.logicojp.reviewer.presentation.CliOutput
 ==> expected: <[]> but was: <[dev.logicojp.reviewer.presentation.CliOutput]>
[ERROR] Tests run: 10, Failures: 1, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0
[INFO] BUILD FAILURE
```

**After revert** (`git diff` on `CliOutput.java` clean):

```
[arch] Rule 5b (presentation ⊥ infrastructure)            69 classes inspected, 0 violator(s), 0 exempt
[INFO] Tests run: 10, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0
```

The rule fires, names the offending class, and fails the build.

## G2 — Correlation logging restored as a port

### Why it vanished

MDC is thread-local. `ExecutorService.submit()` and `StructuredTaskScope.fork()` start child
threads with an **empty** MDC, so `%X{execution.id}` in the logback pattern rendered blank for
every agent-execution and rubber-duck log line. t13 deleted the propagation helpers from
`util.ExecutionCorrelation` rather than migrating them, and **no test noticed**, because no test
asserted the capability existed.

### The fix

```
application/port/outbound/PropagateCorrelationPort   ← declares the capability (imports: shared + java.util only)
infrastructure/logging/MdcCorrelationAdapter         ← @Singleton, org.slf4j.MDC implementation
```

This keeps `application` free of any logging-framework import (Rule 5 stays at 0 violators)
while the capability itself lives where the framework coupling belongs.

Wiring — port threaded from the composition root down to both loss sites:

```
ReviewCommand ─┐
               ├─ ReviewOrchestratorFactory ─ ReviewOrchestrator ─┬─ AgentReviewExecutor        (2× submit)
MdcCorrelationAdapter (@Singleton) ─────────────────────────────  └─ ReviewExecutionModeRunner (1× fork)
```

`ReviewCommand` lost its raw `import org.slf4j.MDC;` and now calls
`propagateCorrelation.bindExecutionId(...)` / `.clearExecutionId()`.

### Two deliberate design choices

1. **No `noOp()` factory on the port.** A no-op default is *exactly* how the capability
   disappeared the first time — code compiled, tests passed, logs went blank. There is one
   implementation and tests use the real `MdcCorrelationAdapter`, so every assertion is honest.
2. **`callWithContext` restores the previous context in a `finally`.** Virtual/pooled carrier
   threads must never be left carrying another task's correlation ID. Covered by
   `restoresContextEvenWhenSupplierThrows`.

### Tests added (15 new)

| Test | Guards |
|---|---|
| `AgentReviewExecutorTest.propagatesExecutionIdToAgentExecutionThread` | `submit()` boundary #1 |
| `AgentReviewExecutorTest.propagatesExecutionIdToRubberDuckThread` | `submit()` boundary #2 |
| `ReviewExecutionModeRunnerTest.propagatesExecutionIdToStructuredTasks` | `StructuredTaskScope.fork()` boundary |
| `MdcCorrelationAdapterTest` (10 tests) | bind / blank-clears / selective clear / detached copy / null-when-empty / cross-thread carry / restore / restore-on-throw / null-context / current-context |
| `PropagateCorrelationPortWiringTest` | the container actually binds the port to `MdcCorrelationAdapter` |

The three propagation tests each assert the child ran on a **different thread name** than the
caller — without that, the assertion could pass vacuously if the work were ever inlined.

`PropagateCorrelationPortWiringTest` is the one that stops this regressing again: unit tests only
prove the executors *use* whatever port they are handed; resolving the bean from a real
`ApplicationContext` proves production hands them one.

## G3 — Duplicate utilities consolidated

Deleted `infrastructure/config/ConfigDefaults` and `infrastructure/auth/RetryPolicyUtils`;
`shared/` copies are now the only definitions. 12 call sites repointed (10 config records,
`CopilotClientStarter`, `GhAuthTokenProvider`).

### ⚠️ The two `RetryPolicyUtils` were **not** equivalent

Plain deletion would have silently changed retry behaviour. The divergence:

| | infrastructure copy | shared copy |
|---|---|---|
| transient markers | `connection reset`, `timeout`, `unavailable`, `stream closed`, `broken pipe` | `timeout`, `temporarily`, `rate limit`, `too many requests`, `429`, `503`, `connection reset`, `network` |
| `InterruptedException` | explicit `→ false` | **absent** |
| null root cause | null-safe | **would NPE** |

**Resolution:** merged the **union** of markers plus the `InterruptedException` guard plus
null-safety into `shared/RetryPolicyUtils`, with provenance comments on each marker group.
This is strictly a superset for the two former `shared` consumers
(`application/review/ReviewRetryExecutor`, `shared/RetryExecutor`) — a documented, accepted
behaviour widening, not a silent narrowing.

`ConfigDefaults` was genuinely identical (the infrastructure copy only added SLF4J debug
logging); `ConfigDefaults.class.getClassLoader()` resolves to the same app classloader either
way. Note `shared/ConfigDefaults` had **zero** importers before this task — it was dead code
until the 10 records were repointed to it.

## Deliberate non-change

`presentation/CliSecurityAudit` still imports `org.slf4j.MDC` directly. This is **not** a G2
leak and **not** a Rule 5b violation:

- Rule 5b forbids `presentation → dev.logicojp.reviewer.infrastructure`. SLF4J is a third-party
  library; presentation is the outermost layer and already carries picocli and DI annotations.
- Its MDC use is *same-thread scoped audit fields* via `putCloseable` try-with-resources — it
  never crosses a thread boundary, so the propagation port does not apply.
- ADR-0006 records the explicit decision that routing a single CLI-originated audit statement
  through an application outbound port was disproportionate.

Flagged here so t17 review does not read it as an inconsistency.
